questions.text: Which keyword is used to define an interface in TypeScript?
questions.explanation: The `interface` keyword is used to define a structural contract for objects.

questions.text: What is the purpose of the 'any' type?
questions.explanation: 'any' allows a variable to hold any value and bypasses TypeScript's type checking.

questions.text: How do you specify that a property is optional in an interface?
questions.explanation: Appending a `?` to the property name in an interface or type makes it optional.

questions.text: Which of these is a valid way to define a generic function?
questions.explanation: Generic functions use angle brackets `<T>` to declare a type parameter.

questions.text: What is the output of a TypeScript compilation?
questions.explanation: TypeScript is transpiled into standard JavaScript code.

questions.text: Which modifier makes a class member accessible only within the class?
questions.explanation: `private` members are only accessible within the class they are defined in.

questions.explanation: Tuples allow you to express an array where the type of a fixed number of elements is known.

questions.text: How do you define a union type?
questions.explanation: The pipe symbol `|` is used to define a union type.

A type that can only be null
questions.explanation: 'unknown' is safer than 'any' because it requires type checking before performing operations on the value.

questions.text: Which utility type makes all properties of an object optional?
questions.explanation: `Partial<T>` constructs a type with all properties of T set to optional.

questions.text: What is the difference between an interface and a type alias?
questions.explanation: Interfaces are primarily used for defining object shapes and support declaration merging. Type aliases are more flexible and can represent primitives, unions, and intersections, but don't support merging.
It's a pattern where you use a common property (literal type) in multiple interfaces within a union to allow TypeScript to narrow down the specific type in a switch or if block.

questions.text: How does 'Structural Typing' work in TypeScript?
questions.explanation: TypeScript uses structural typing, meaning if two objects have the same shape (members and types), they are considered to be of the same type, regardless of their explicit declarations.
They are files used to provide type information for JavaScript libraries that don't have built-in TypeScript support, allowing the compiler to understand the external code's structure.

questions.text: Describe the purpose of the 'never' type.
questions.explanation: 'never' represents the type of values that never occur, such as the return type of a function that always throws an exception or one that has an infinite loop.
